recommendation: Keep the commit as-is. It completes the published terminology clarification across current build-scoped narrative without broadening the issue to unrelated uses of "wire" such as transport prose.
issue_request: FHIR-12435 was a Published/Persuasive FHIR-core clarification asking to replace "Wire format" with "Serialization format" in the formats page section 2.21.0.1.4 and elsewhere if necessary because "wire format" was not widely understood outside HL7.
initial_application: Historical commit 02cee392327706bfee65e3749abfc0762ca9803f applied #12435 to the main formats-related pages and related source artifacts. Current source no longer had the phrase on the original formats page family, but still had two build-scoped narrative uses in Basic and Signatures.
additional_context: The Basic occurrence predated the original 2017 application and was missed there; Basic is active in source/fhir.ini. The Signatures occurrence was introduced later during the 2025 signatures rewrite, and signatures.html is included in source/hierarchy.xml. Zulip discussion confirmed "serialization format" as the intended replacement term, and Confluence refs search found no conflicting record.
reconciliation: Changed source/basic/basic-introduction.xml to say Basic is compatible with FHIR serialization formats, and source/signatures.html to refer to resource serialization formats instead of wire formats. Historical release cache files and the DefinitionUse code/display "wire-format" were left untouched because they are historical/generated or code-system content rather than current narrative wording.
source_changes: source/basic/basic-introduction.xml: replaced "wire-format compatible" with "compatible with FHIR serialization formats".
source/signatures.html: replaced "wire formats (JSON and XML)" with "serialization formats (JSON and XML)".
